summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would rewrite the rules for how agricultural levies, customs charges and services levies are set and collected.
The package would replace five existing Acts and let the government set levy rates and conditions through regulations rather than primary legislation.
The explanatory memorandum says the current system has more than 50 pieces of legislation covering over 110 levies across more than 75 commodities and 18 levy recipient bodies.
changes: Replace five existing levy and charge imposition Acts with three new bills.
Allow excise levies and customs charges on primary industry produce to be re-established in regulations.
Enable levies on goods used in animal, plant, fungus or algae maintenance or treatment, including the horse disease response levy.
Allow excise levies on goods used in nursery product production or preparation.
Enable regulations to impose levies on services that help produce primary industry products, such as commercial bee pollination.
Provide a consistent framework across the three bills for definitions, exemptions, rates and other common matters.
summary.affected: Farmers, producers, processors, exporters and agricultural, fisheries and forestry industries that pay or are affected by agricultural levies and charges.

Mr Littleproud [explained that](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2023-11-15.151.2): > *This set of amendments will add to the [Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Bill 2023](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r7091) by clarifying, affirming and solidifying the essential roles that Animal Health Australia—the AHA—and Plant Health Australia—the PHA—have within our levy framework. The AHA represents 14 livestock industries while the PHA represents 39 plant industry members. They need to remain important players in this space. These two levy organisations are levy recipient bodies, and they are responsible for facilitating industry-government partnerships for pest and disease preparedness, prevention, emergency response and management. However, under the provisions of the government's bill, references to the AHA levy and the PHA levy have been renamed as the 'biosecurity activity levy'.
